packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure: none. Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading.
Beyond the rules: I made rotated/enlarged crops (Python PIL, written to a separate scratch folder, not in the packet) of the upside-down strips in image-001 and image-003 and of the German cursive strip in image-001, to read them the right way up. No other files, directories, web, or search used. All five images loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 (overview, face A): binding strips (parchment guards/stubs) mounted on dark board around a spine stub.
  * Upper strip: mounted UPSIDE DOWN. After rotation it shows two columns of a ruled book-hand (textualis) page with a fold/blank gutter between: left column with neumes (unheighted, staffless, adiastematic-looking) over short sung text lines, plus prayer text; a red rubric "...ps(alm?)/xi" with red initial S and a red "a" before a black-ruled initial D; right column has a red initial C (Consisto/Confitto?) mid-column. Interpretation: a liturgical (missal/gradual-type) leaf with neumed chants and prayers.
  * Lower left strip: two lines of a large textualis (black) at the top edge, cut off below; small fragment of another column at far left ("...ple / ...n apl(or)um"). Rest blank parchment (lower margin).
  * Lower right strip (image-001, rotated ~90 deg as mounted): later German cursive (Kurrent-type) in brown ink, ca. 12 lines, a different, later document.
- image-002: native tile of the lower-left large-script strip.
- image-003 (overview, face B): upper strip mounted UPSIDE DOWN; one column of ruled textualis prose, 7 lines plus a neumed line at the (rotated) bottom with red "a" and initial D; red "cap" marginal; sewing thread obscures the right end. Lower strip: red rubric line in large textualis "...ascensione domini" and a large red initial P at the right in the next column; otherwise blank.
- image-004: tile of the red initial P (lower strip of image-003); faint marks at right edge (pen trials or cropped text, unreadable).
- image-005: tile of the red rubric "...ascensione domin(i)" with sewing threads over the start.

TRANSCRIPTIONS
Line numbers for upside-down strips are counted in reading order after rotating 180 deg (i.e. from the top of the rotated strip), since the strip is inverted in the image. Neume rows are noted but not transcribed.

image-001, upper strip, left column (rotated):
 1  [neumes]
 2  [r]egulus cuius filius infir[-]
 3  [neumes]
 4  [..]  in galileam rogabat eum
 5  q(ue)s(umus) d(omi)ne co(n)tinua pietate
 6  [..]era (et) i(n) bonis actib(us) tuo
 7  [..]natura(m) ter(?) ut possitis
 8  [red:] ps(alm?)/xi(?)  [red initial] S  umentes scutum   (read "Sumentes scutum"; macron over first minims)
 9  [ex]tinguere . [red] a(ntiphona?)  [initial] D  omine   [neumes above "Domine"]
 Note: line 4 has a neume row above; line 7 "natura(m) ter(?)" uncertain - first letters cut at gutter.
image-001, upper strip, right column (rotated; right edge cut):
 1  cui uxorem[...]
 2  (et) malas cog[...]
 3  sic (et) uxore(m) [...]
 4  tat dece(m) mi[...]
 5  miserit . n(on)(?) [...]
 6  [red initial C] onfisto(?) / Consto(?) i(n) d[...]    (initial is a red C; read "Confido i(n) d[omino]"? - letters after C look like "onfido" or "onfito", uncertain)
 7  diem xpi ihu[...]   (diem Christi Iesu)

image-002 / image-001 lower-left strip (large textualis, upright):
 left fragment col:
 1  [..]ple
 2  [..]n aplo(rum)
 main col:
 1  omnia que(m)(?) dedisti[...]   (over "que" an abbreviation stroke; "dedisti" partly cut, read "dedi[sti]" ; last letters cut by fold)
 2  te sunt q(ui)a(?) / q(uia) u(er)ba q(ue) de[...]   ("te sunt q(uia) u(er)ba q(ue) de[...]"; "u(er)ba" with stroke over u)
 Below: blank (lower margin). Unread: nothing else visible.

image-003, upper strip (rotated 180 deg; right end under sewing threads):
 0  [cropped descenders/ascenders of a line above, illegible]
 1  (et) filios uenundatos p(er)seuerante illo i(n) malitia . i(n)sipientia(m)
 2  [co]gitationes intelligi uolu(n)t(?) . [red-touched S] ic enim iusti uxor dicit[ur?] [threads] [..]
 3  [..]iusti (et) peccatoris appellari stultitia(m) . [red-touched S] ed q(uonia)m d(omi)n(u)s [threads]
 4  [..]a talenta . (et) ille nobis co(n)seruus suus centu(m) denarios [threads]
 5  [e]cclesiastice int(er)pretationis e(st) . n(on) a prudentib(us) iuris re[threads]
 6  [..]o ihu quia qui cepit i(n) uobis op(us) bonu(m) p(er)ficiet usq(ue) i(n)   [red, margin:] cap
 7  [..] . [red] a(ntiphona?)  [initial] D  ixit autem dominus seruo redde quod debes [..]   [neume row above; lower half of letters cut]
 Notes: line 2 "uolu(n)t" could be "uoluit"; line 2 end "dicitur sapientia(?)" partly visible through threads - uncertain, not supplied.

image-003 lower strip / image-005 / image-004:
 1  [red] [D]e(?) ascensione domini   (start covered by threads; "[..]ascensione domin[i]")
 next column: large red initial P, no following text visible. Faint marks at right edge of image-004 (possibly letters "s", "x" in later ink) - unreadable.

image-001 lower-right strip, German cursive (rotated ~90 deg; read with enlarged crop). Very uncertain; left/right edges cut:
 1  [...]
 2  [..]braut (?) Dind ha(?)[...]
 3  "tel der rudern(?) [...]
 4  b(?) d(?) / Sen achte(?) d[...]
 5  rudern(?) und ain[...]
 6  kerb(?) gegen Bitter(?)[...]
 7  urtube(?) zu Rad ha[...]
 8  der rudern und a[...]
 9  gat Brem(?) Leim(?)[...]
10  Schreibsch(?) mer(?)[...]
11  von Dolms(?) i(?) R[...]
12  und ain halb kirch(?)[...]
13  Drain(?) und halb a[...]
14  ain rudern(?)
 This is a later German-language hand; readings above are low-confidence letter-by-letter guesses (recurring word looks like "rudern"/"ruder", and "und ain").

UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Both liturgical strips are cut at the fold/gutter and edges; the right ends of image-003 lines 2-6 are under sewing threads.
- Neumes not transcribed.
- image-003 line 0 and line 7 lower halves cut.
- German cursive strip only partially legible; a higher-resolution tile of that strip would help. No native tile of the image-001 upper strip or image-003 upper strip was supplied; native tiles would improve the prose readings.
- Possible relation: the image-001 upper strip and image-003 upper strip look like the same hand and ruling (could be two faces/parts of one leaf), but I cannot confirm.
